title: The New Job Market: Hiring, Hunting, and AI in the Middle
description:
This session looks at how AI is reshaping every stage of the job hunt - from the CV that gets written, to the screening system that reads it, to the interview on the other side, to the market candidates are landing in.

The focus is practical and aimed at job seekers, career changers, and anyone trying to make sense of how hiring actually works now - but recruiters, hiring managers, and HR folks will get plenty out of it too.

We'll explore-

* The current challenges, specifically in the Auckland NZ marketplace
* Writing CVs and cover letters with AI - what works, what flags as generic, and how to keep your voice
* Getting past the bots - how applicant tracking systems and AI screeners actually evaluate applications
* The new interview landscape - AI-assisted screening calls, async video interviews, and live AI note-takers
* Interview prep with AI - mock interviews, company research, and rehearsing tough questions
* Where AI helps you stand out vs. where it makes everyone sound the same
* Job market shifts - which roles are growing, shrinking, or changing shape, and what that means for positioning
* Building an AI-resilient career - skills, signals, and portfolios that hold their value
* Spotting fake jobs, scam recruiters, and AI-generated postings
* Practical workflows and tools that are actually worth using

After these sessions we typically grab dinner nearby if you want to keep the conversation going and connect with other professionals.

title: Mindfulness meditation
location: Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tāmaki, Wellesley Street East, Auckland Central, Auckland, Auckland
description:
Join Fiona for a gentle and welcoming introduction to mindfulness meditation in Forever Tomorrow: Chinese Art Now.
Like the practices explored by artists Lu Pingyuan, Lin Ke and Lu Yang, mindful meditation approaches perception as a field of hidden forces, quiet revelations and continuous transformation.
This one-hour session is designed especially for people who are curious about meditation or just beginning their practice - even if you feel like you ‘can’t sit still’ or your mind is often busy.
Fiona will begin by introducing the foundations of mindfulness, sharing simple insights into what meditation is (and what it isn’t). She will offer practical guidance on working with common challenges such as physical discomfort and a wandering mind.
The session will include a few gentle chair-based movements to warm up the body and prepare for sitting comfortably. From there, you’ll be guided into a calming mindfulness meditation, allowing you to experience moments of stillness, clarity and ease.
No previous meditation experience is required - just curiosity and a willingness to explore.
About Fiona Liu
Fiona Liu is the founder of Mindfully Yin Yoga School and a highly experienced yoga and mindfulness teacher with nearly two decades of teaching experience.
Her work is dedicated to helping people slow down, reconnect with themselves and cultivate awareness through mindful movement and meditation. Fiona has trained and mentored many yoga teachers and students over the years. She is deeply passionate about making meditation accessible and approachable for everyone.

恰如艺术家陆平原、林科和陆扬在他们的艺术创作中探索的——正念冥想将感知世界视为一个带有隐秘力量与默然启示，且持续变化着的场域。
纵然你觉得自己平时“坐不住”，你的思绪也常常停不下来——若你对冥想感兴趣，或刚刚开始接触冥想，那么这场一个小时的活动就是为你量身打造的。
Fiona会首先介绍正念的基础知识，分享关于何为冥想（以及什么不是冥想）的简要认知，并就如何应对身体不适和心神不定等常见生活挑战提供实用的指导。

title: An Introduction To Stoic Ethics
location: 37 Normanby Road, Mount Eden, Auckland 1024, Auckland
description:
E te whanau tena koutou katoa.
Ethics is about what is morally good and bad or right and wrong. The stoics believed that everyone has the capacity for reason and they appealed to reason in debating ethical issues. We will be looking at some of the ethical ideas of three ancient stoic philosophers as follows
1.**Chrisippus of Sol** (280-206 BCE) was the third leader and sometimes called the “second founder of Stoicism” for his contributions to the developing philosophy. He clarified and debated stoic ideas.
Chrisippus was a runner before he took over the Athens school of philosophy. His name means “Golden Horse”. A quote of his: **“*Runners in a race ought to compete and strive to win as hard as they can but by no means should they trip their competitors or give them a shove. So to in life, it is not wrong to seek after the things useful in life; but to do so while depriving someone else is not just”***
Chrisippus wrote a book called *On Passions* concerning the therapy of the emotions. He believed human nature is ethical in accordance with nature and reason and that one can achieve freedom from irrational desires or passions such as greed pride lust through applying reason and understanding the harm they cause.
**2**. **Antipator of Tarsus** (2nd century BC) Had some differences with Diogenes who he replaced as leader of the stoa. He taught concepts of moral duty in every day life e.g. the duty of honest disclosure, family values and rational decision making. He invited people over to dinner to have long discussions about philosophy as told in a book called “*The Learned Banquetiers*” by Athenaeus.
**3** .**Hierocles** (2nd century CE). wrote a book called *Elements of Ethics* not much of which is preserved apart from an interesting description of individuals in a series of circles beginning with the human mind, then immediate family followed by extended family then local community then neighbouring towns followed by country then the entire human race. title: The New Web: AI, Agents, and the Shifting Stack
description:
This session covers the rapidly shifting intersection of AI and the web - how sites get built, how they get found, and how the tooling around design and development is changing month to month.

The focus will lean towards web developers, designers, and digital marketers, but the shifts we'll explore - from discovery to delivery - affect anyone with a stake in their organization's web presence.
We'll explore-

* The Google I/O 2026 announcements - what's new, what matters, and what to ignore
* AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) - how content gets surfaced by ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and the next wave of answer engines
* Agentic considerations - designing sites for AI agents that browse, click, and transact on behalf of users
* How AEO and agentic discovery reshape (or don't reshape) the traditional SEO playbook
* AI-assisted web development - from copilots to full agentic coding workflows
* New design tools - what's emerged, what's worth adopting, and what's still hype
* Design considerations in an AI-first web - when interfaces are generated, summarized, or skipped entirely
* Practical experiments, prototypes, and what's actually shipping

After these sessions we typically grab dinner nearby if you want to keep the conversation going and connect with other professionals.
